summary.oneLiner: A very strong, capital-flush quarter: PAT +59.8% to INR3,444.56cr, NII +33.7% to INR8,055.70cr and NIM at a peak 9.04%  — turbo-charged by the ~INR39,600cr equity infusion (April 2026) that added ~INR500cr of NII, cut leverage to 2.14x (from 3.82x) and lifted CAR to 34.1%. Disbursements +19.5% and AUM +15.3% YoY  on a GST-cut-driven auto up-cycle, with used/new-CV demand resilient despite the West-Asia war. Management reaffirms an **18% FY27 growth** guide , a medium-term normalisation of NIM to ~8.5% as new-vehicle mix rises, ~2% credit-cost, and outsized gold/MSME expansion. Asset quality stable . The one debate: whether the ~9% NIM can be held vs management's deliberately conservative 8.5% medium-term guide.

one-line thesis: A very strong, capital-flush quarter: PAT +59.8% to INR3,444.56cr, NII +33.7% to INR8,055.70cr and NIM at a peak 9.04% (vs 8.11% YoY / 8.61% QoQ) — turbo-charged by the ~INR39,600cr equity infusion (April 2026) that added ~INR500cr of NII, cut leverage to 2.14x (from 3.82x) and lifted CAR to 34.1%. Disbursements +19.5% and AUM +15.3% YoY (INR3.14 lakh cr) on a GST-cut-driven auto up-cycle, with used/new-CV demand resilient despite the West-Asia war. Management reaffirms an **18% FY27 growth** guide (Q2 ≥15%, will reassess post-monsoon), a medium-term normalisation of NIM to ~8.5% as new-vehicle mix rises, ~2% credit-cost, and outsized gold/MSME expansion. Asset quality stable (GS3 4.64%). The one debate: whether the ~9% NIM can be held vs management's deliberately conservative 8.5% medium-term guide.
financial scorecard (track qoq/yoy):
| Metric | Q1 FY27 | YoY | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| Disbursements | INR49,974.49cr | +19.51% (vs INR41,816.75cr) | CV INR19,556cr / PV INR11,018cr / MSME INR6,184cr / gold INR5,153cr / 2W INR3,548cr / PL INR2,773cr / farm INR947cr / CE INR792cr |
| AUM | INR3,13,798.39cr | +15.26% (QoQ +3.81%) | vs INR2,72,249cr YoY; INR3,02,274cr Q4FY26 |
| NII | INR8,055.70cr | +33.67% (vs INR6,026.43cr) | Incl. ~INR500cr from surplus capital |
| NIM | 9.04% | +93bps (vs 8.11%); +43bps QoQ (8.61%) | Peak; guided to normalise to ~8.5% medium term |
| PAT | INR3,444.56cr | +59.79% (vs INR2,155.7cr) | Q4FY26 was INR3,013.57cr; EPS INR14.83 (vs INR11.46) |
| Asset quality | GS3 4.64% / NS3 2.33% | vs 4.53%/2.57% YoY; 4.58%/2.33% QoQ | GS3 nudged up (seasonal); credit cost 1.66% of assets (1.64% YoY / 1.68% QoQ) |
| Cost-to-income | 25.48% | vs 29.29% FY26; 25.32% Q4FY26 | Stable/low |
| Capital & leverage | CAR 34.1%; leverage 2.14x | vs 3.82x (Mar) | Post ~INR39,600cr April-2026 raise; LCR 262.54% (~6 mo repayment cover) |
> One-offs distorting the headline: the April-2026 **equity infusion** is the master variable — it (a) added ~INR500cr NII (which "will gradually subside"), (b) let the company repay ~INR18,000cr of liabilities (total liabilities INR2,50,690cr→INR2,32,639cr) rather than grow, temporarily depressing leverage/gearing, and (c) inflated NIM/ROA optically. Cost of funds fell only 3bps (8.59%→8.56%) but incremental cost is 7.77% and improving on a ratings upgrade (no longer priced as AA).
guidance (critical — verify next quarter:
- **AUM/loan growth:** **FY27 ~18%** (earlier guidance holds; will revise after Q2 once monsoon impact is clear). **Q2FY27 ≥15%**, accelerating in H2 if conditions improve.
- **NIM:** hold at ~current (~9%) for the immediate 2 quarters (capital deployment); **normalise to ~8.5% over the medium term (2-3 yr)** as lower-yield new-vehicle mix rises and cost benefit is passed to borrowers.
- **Credit cost:** ~**2%** near and medium term (currently running below at 1.66%).
- **Cost-to-income:** stable (branch/manpower adds absorbed by volume).
- **Gold book:** **double in 3 years, ~2.5%→~5% of book** (2,200 branches gold-enabled).
- **New-vehicle mix:** disbursement share 16%→20-25%; **new-vehicle book to 30%+** of total (medium term).
- **MSME:** ~15%→~20% of book; growth **above** the 18% company average.
- **CV:** ~15% growth for FY27.
- **Branches:** ~**150 added** in FY27.
- **Funding:** no further liability repayment; deploy surplus liquidity into growth over ~1-1.5 months, then resume fresh borrowing / securitization toward quarter-end.
order book & pipeline: Not an order-book model — forward view keyed to auto sales + rural income. Q1FY27 industry volumes (management-cited): CV +14.1%, M&HCV +18.3%, LCV +20.8%, PV +25.9%, 2W +20.3%, 3W +29.7%, tractors +21.6%, construction equipment +8.8% (first positive after a negative FY). EV sales surged (2W +69.3%, PV +94.8%). GST rate cut is the demand catalyst. Disbursement pipeline healthy across segments; construction-equipment disbursal (~INR1,000cr for 5 quarters) expected to re-accelerate toward its old ~INR2,000cr run-rate from next quarter.
segment / subsidiary detail:
- **Commercial Vehicles (core):** INR19,556cr disbursed; growth "in line with ~20% market" — used-CV demand from rural market strong; no vehicle idling / stress seen despite fuel worries.
- **New vehicle:** ~16% of disbursement and rising — driven by existing-customer upgrades and win-back of customers lost when SFL couldn't match rates (now can, on lower funding cost + capital).
- **Passenger Vehicles:** INR11,018cr.
- **Gold:** INR5,153cr; ~2.5% of book, 2,200 branches enabled; targeted to double to ~5% in 3 years (see §6).
- **MSME:** INR6,184cr; ~15% of book, historically South-concentrated, now rolling out West→North/East (hub-and-spoke processing). Inflection underway; growth to beat company average.
- **2-Wheelers** INR3,548cr; **Personal Loans** INR2,773cr (kept within known customers, limited outsourcing); **Farm** INR947cr; **Construction Equipment** INR792cr.
growth verticals / optionality:
- **Gold-loan scale-up** — the clearest optionality: existing branch network repurposed (2,200 ready), riding the shift of borrowers from unsecured/hand-loans and pawnbrokers to gold-backed credit; target 2x book in 3 years.
- **MSME geographic expansion** beyond the South — long runway ("a lot of scope"), gated by hiring specialised manpower in North/Central.
- **New-vehicle penetration** of the existing customer base — larger ticket sizes structurally lift disbursement growth.
- **Cross-sell of personal loans** to gold/MSME customers (previously only 2-wheeler customers).
margins & cost dynamics: NIM 9.04% is a capital-inflated peak; ~INR500cr of the NII is surplus-capital income that decays as liquidity is deployed. Management guides operational NIM to ~8.5% medium term — an analyst (Chintan) pushed back that this looks conservative given slow mix-shift; management held the line ("we've always been conservative"). Funding tailwind: incremental cost 7.77% vs 8.56% on-book; ratings-driven repricing benefit as SFL is no longer borrowed-for as an AA entity. Cost-to-income low at 25.48%; incremental branch/manpower cost to be absorbed by volume.
capex / expansion (watch slippage): Physical expansion = ~150 branches in FY27 + manpower (esp. specialised MSME staff for North/Central). No heavy capex; the "expansion" is balance-sheet growth funded by the capital raise and resumed borrowing/securitization from quarter-end.
capital allocation: Post ~INR39,600cr April-2026 raise, the quarter's priority was **deleveraging** — ~INR18,000cr of high-cost liabilities repaid (leverage 3.82x→2.14x, CAR 34.1%). That phase is now "done": no further repayment; surplus liquidity (kept ~3 months / ~INR17,000-18,000cr of repayment cover) to be deployed into growth over ~1-1.5 months, then fresh borrowing including securitization/direct-assignment resumes. Off-balance-sheet share fell simply because no securitization was done this quarter (not demand-led).
risks & watch-items:
- **Monsoon/El-Nino:** seasonal rainfall ~24% below normal (Jun 4-Jul 16); management explicitly **waiting for Q2** to judge rural-income/agri-output impact before confirming the 18% guide — the key swing factor.
- **West-Asia war / fuel:** feared steep fuel-price spike didn't materialise; one-time cost pass-through "already absorbed"; E20 ethanol norm reduces import dependence. Residual risk if retail fuel spikes further.
- **NIM normalisation:** structural glide to 8.5% as new-vehicle mix rises — near-term supported by surplus capital, but the ~INR500cr capital-NII tailwind fades.
- **Asset quality:** GS3 nudged up (4.58%→4.64%; +18% YoY in Stage-3 assets flagged by an analyst) — management calls it seasonal, not stress; gold Stage-2/3 forward-flows to watch (bullet→interest-servicing migration).
- **E20 durability** debate on used cars — management downplays (OEMs certify E20; SFL finances cars <7yr, trucks unaffected).
management quality / tone: Confident and deliberately conservative — repeatedly defers full-year upgrades to post-Q2 monsoon clarity while expressing comfort on demand. Transparent on the capital-raise mechanics (deleveraging first, growth next) and willing to be pushed on the 8.5% NIM guide without caving. Macro-heavy opening (GDP/inflation/auto volumes) frames the cyclical tailwind. IR-responsive (offers offline data splits).
non-obvious takeaways:
- The quarter's optics are a **capital-raise artefact**: ~INR500cr of NII, the leverage collapse to 2.14x, the 34.1% CAR and part of the 9% NIM all trace to the April infusion — normalise for it before trend-lining PAT/NIM.
- **Deleveraging, not slow growth, explains falling liabilities/off-book** — a temporary, now-complete phase; expect borrowing + securitization to resume from quarter-end (a re-leveraging growth signal).
- The **8.5% medium-term NIM guide is a choice** (pass funding benefit to borrowers to win new-vehicle share), not a forced compression — the real question is mix-shift speed (new-vehicle 16%→30%+).
- **Gold + MSME are the mix-changers**: both guided to grow faster than the 18% average, gradually diversifying SFL away from its CV core.
